ud8.10:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud8.10:1.3: There it was that the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
ud8.10:1.4: “Monks!” “Reverend Sir!” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
ud8.10:1.6: and the Fortunate One said this:
ud8.10:2.1: “While venerable Dabba Mallaputta, monks - after going up into the sky, and sitting in cross-legged posture in the air, in the firmament, entering the fire-element, and emerging, - was attaining Complete Emancipation, his body burning and being consumed, there was no charcoal and no ash evident.
ud8.10:2.2: Just as while ghee or oil is burning and being consumed there is no charcoal and no ash evident,
ud8.10:2.3: so also while venerable Dabba Mallaputta - after going up into the sky, and sitting in cross-legged posture in the air, in the firmament, entering the fire-element, and emerging - was attaining Complete Emancipation, his body burning and being consumed, there was no charcoal and no ash evident.”
ud8.10:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud8.10:4.2: ~ which is struck by fire and heat,
ud8.10:4.4: ~ the destiny (of that heat) is not known,
ud8.10:5.1: So it is for those perfectly free,
ud8.10:5.2: ~ who have crossed over the flood of bondage to sense pleasures:
ud8.10:5.4: ~ for those who have attained unagitated happiness.”
